questions: When moving pieces simultaneously one square closer to square i, what happens to pieces that are already at square i? Do they stay in place, or are they considered to have moved zero distance and remain?
If a piece is at the leftmost square (square 1) and we choose i=1, does it stay at square 1? Similarly, if a piece is at square N and we choose i=N, does it stay?

When moving pieces closer to square i, if a piece is to the left of i, it moves right; if to the right, it moves left. What if i is between two squares? Since i is an integer, it's a specific square, so pieces move toward that square's position.

Is the operation allowed to be performed even if it would cause pieces to move out of bounds (e.g., a piece at square 1 moving left when i=2)? Since moving closer to i from the left means moving right, there's no out-of-bounds, but what about i=1 and a piece at square 1? It stays, so no out-of-bounds issue.
Are pieces indistinguishable? That is, does the configuration only care about the set of squares with at least one piece, not which specific pieces are where?
Can we choose the same i multiple times consecutively? Is there any restriction on the sequence of i values?
For the minimum number of operations, if multiple sequences achieve the target, do we count the number of operations in the shortest sequence? Or is there a different optimization criterion?

If B has a 1 in a square where A has a 0, but there are no pieces initially, is it always impossible? Not necessarily, because pieces can move. But what if B requires a piece in a square that no piece can ever reach due to movement constraints?
